column2: Around our lands more people speak this new tongue, but some most observant elders of society speak in whispers that such a tongue seem eerily familar to an ancient tongue long thought forgotten. I find this name they speak of "Brythonic" a much pleasing name indeed. Perhaps this tongue is even more prestigious than one thought? We continue to use our own influence to promote this means of communication in the interests of a more efficient realm.

Although every civilized man knows that the venerable Celtic Tongue is the true language of communication, this new tongue does have a certain functionality. I have therefore prevailed upon a member of my court to adopt this for everyday administrative use.

I was considering important business when I had an amazing insight. To strengthen my realm I must bring my vassals round to my way of thinking. This involves communication. If I can get them to communicate like me then I will have a much smoother running realm.

As your child is soon of age you can choose to hold a grand Navjote for [Root.GetHerHim], inviting your vassals and the members of your court. This can help build trust that will certainly prove useful for the child in the future.

The day of [navjote_target.GetBestName]'s Navjote is soon approaching, and excitement builds in the palace. Your Magi [Root.job_spiritual.GetBestName] has offered to personally prepare [navjote_target.GetHerHim] in the final month, to understand the Ahuna Vairya so that they are prepared to give their oath.
I can prepare [navjote_target.GetBestName] for the Navjote myself!
[navjote_target.GetBestName] can figure it out on [navjote_target.GetHerHis] own.

The day has arrived. At your family's atashgah [navjote_target.GetBestName] approaches the atar brimming with a regal confidence. [navjote_target.GetSheHeCap] reads [navjote_target.GetHerHis] Ahuna Vairya portion effortlessly, followed by a statement of faith, din no kalmo, with a conviction that impresses even the most cynical of your vassals.

The day has arrived. At your family's atashgah [navjote_target.GetBestName] approaches the atar shaking nervously. [navjote_target.GetSheHeCap] stumbles [navjote_target.GetHerHis] way through the passage, constantly stopping for corrections from an uneased samaritan. Your vassals cringe in pity as [navjote_target.GetFirstName] attempts to deliver a clumsy statement of faith clearly written the night before.

In the celebration after, you see [navjote_target.GetBestName] and [compliment_vassal.GetBestName] discussing intently some issue brought up in [navjote_target.GetHerHis] Avesta like the sayings of Zarathustra, with [navjote_target.GetFirstName] displaying a maturity you didn't realize [navjote_target.GetSheHe] had. Afterwards [compliment_vassal.GetFirstName] pull you aside to tell you just how impressed [compliment_vassal.GetSheHe] is.

In the celebration after, you see [navjote_target.GetBestName] and [insult_vassal.GetBestName] arguing, when [navjote_target.GetFirstName] suddenly jumps up out of [navjote_target.GetHerHis] seat, flailing at [insult_vassal.GetFirstName] until your guards are able to pull [navjote_target.GetHerHim] away. [insult_vassal.GetFirstName] calls out to you: "is this how your family treats guests?".

It seems as if [navjote_target.GetFirstName] has started getting along incredibly well with the child of one of the visiting vassals! Indeed, apparently [navjote_target.GetFirstName] and [befriended_child.GetBestName] are becoming fast friends.

While having a pleasant conversation you are suddenly interrupted by an infernal ruckus, upon further investigation it seems as if [navjote_target.GetFirstName] has gotten into a fight with the child of one of the visiting vassals! You tear the two children apart, but it is obvious that [navjote_target.GetFirstName] and [rival_child.GetBestName] will not ever be friends after this encounter...

As the hours go by you notice [navjote_target.GetFirstName]'s mood starting to drop. [navjote_target.GetSheHeCap] is obviously still upset about the embarassment at [navjote_target.GetHerHis] Navjote. Hopefully this slump in [navjote_target.GetFirstName]'s mood will pass soon.

After a long night of celebration, the Navjote is finally over. After all the stresses of the day, [navjote_target.GetFirstName] you can't help be see how wonderful they look now that they have don their sudreh and kushti. You bid them farewell as they retire to [navjote_target.GetHerHis] chambers. For better or worse, you look on the child you raised, finally grown to adulthood, and wonder what [navjote_target.GetHerHis] future will bring.
